transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Aurelia CTO), Tom (Aurelia ML), Derek (Aurelia Infra), Sara (PM)

Summary: Quarterly usage/cost/reliability review; agree on a 7-day Dedicated pilot and exchange security docs.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh this is Maya from Redwood. quick agenda, we want to run through usage trends, recent cost spike, reliability incidents, then talk pilot and security handoff.
[00:18] Priya (Aurelia CTO): yep thanks Maya. quick heads up, we've got execs paying attention after the December spending blip so need clear runway and options.
[00:30] Tom (Lead ML Eng): i can show the metrics - our avg token per request is up 22% month over month, but the big kicker is 3 spikes where per-minute qps jumped 4x which blew past our burst limits.
[00:44] Derek (Head of Infra): and for us the autoscale was slow, some requests timed out and the app retried which compounded cost. not great.
[00:55] Omar (Redwood SE): ok got it. when you say retry, is that client-side retries or our fallback kicking in?
[01:05] Tom: mostly client retries, the service tried fallback to a smaller model and that helped but there were token inefficiencies too.
[01:16] Maya: quick question on SLA appetite - would Aurelia consider a Dedicated pool to get predictable throughput?
[01:25] Priya: possibly, but we need to justify cost. execs asked for projected savings and fallback plan if Dedicated hits capacity limits.
[01:36] Maya: fair. we can run a 7-day Dedicated pilot with controlled traffic to show tail latency and unit cost deltas. Omar will size it.
[01:46] Priya: what's the expected percent savings?
[01:50] Omar: for steady-state heavy token workloads we've seen 20-40% per-token cost delta with batching + quantization; if you offload tail to cached prefixes it can be higher, but results depend on your prompt mix.
[02:05] Tom: curious about prefix caching and KV cache -- last time we tried a naive cache it invalidated too often because user prompts changed.
[02:15] Omar: yeah, prefix caching helps when you have repeated system messages or similar prefixes. KV cache is for shorter context reuse across sessions, but it needs stable keys. sometimes transcription or tokenization mismatches make it flaky.
[02:32] Derek: also need to know how cache interacts with private deployments and KMS. data-at-rest restrictions are strict for some datasets.
[02:41] Maya: we support KMS integration on Private and Dedicated. for Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in some regions but i think we should confirm which charts we can provide.
[02:54] Priya: our security team flagged SAML (they wrote SAMEL in the ticket) and SSO integration, plus we need SOC 2 artifacts and network diagram.
[03:06] Maya: we'll send SOC 2, the network diagrams, and SSO guide. i'll include our VPC peering notes and the standard audit log schema.
[03:15] Sara (PM): for success criteria on the pilot, can we define latency P95 and cost per thousand tokens thresholds?
[03:23] Omar: yes, propose we target P95 < 180ms for inference-only endpoints under pilot load and reduce cost per 1k tokens by at least 15% vs current Hosted spend.
[03:35] Tom: acceptable, though we need to ensure metrics are computed the same way (we currently exclude streaming overhead).
[03:44] Maya: we'll align metric definitions in the pilot plan doc.
[03:49] Priya: any mention of fallbacks? in december we lost 2 nodes in a region and the app fell back to a lower-capacity model which returned hallucinations more often.
[03:59] Omar: Redwood has routing policies that can fallback by model variant or region. you can configure weighted canaries and automatic fallback to a smaller model with response monitoring to avoid quality regressions.
[04:15] Derek: is there an automatic circuit breaker to stop retries cascading?
[04:20] Omar: yes, we have per-route circuit breakers; they can fast-fail after X errors and trigger a canary or alternative route. sometimes customers tune it aggressively which can add client-side visible errors, so it's a balance.
[04:35] Tom: another question: quantization profiles - can you recommend a profile that preserves our NER/slot-filling quality?
[04:42] Omar: we can run evals on your test prompts. in our experience 4-bit quantization with per-channel scales keeps downstream NER stable for most transformer decoders, but we'll validate.
[04:55] Priya: ok good. execs will need cost scenarios: pure Hosted growth, mixed Hosted+Dedicated, and Dedicated reserved 12-mo.
[05:05] Maya: i'll send three pricing scenarios and break down unit economics at token and hourly levels.
[05:12] Sara: timeline question: if we start pilot next week, how long to see meaningful numbers?
[05:17] Omar: 7 days of steady traffic gives a decent tail latency and resource utilization readout; if you can run stress windows that mimic peak QPS we'll get better signal.
[05:30] Tom: we can schedule a synthetic peak run on day 3 and 6.
[05:36] Priya: what's the data retention policy in Dedicated vs Hosted? we need to ensure logs and prompts purge after 30 days for some workloads.
[05:45] Maya: Dedicated gives you configurable retention; Hosted defaults 90 days but can be adjusted on enterprise plans. we'll list options in the security pack.
[05:56] Derek: on network: if we use Private (VPC), will Redwood's control plane still see metadata? we need to know what is logged externally.
[06:06] Omar: with Private deployment, control plane is optional — some customers run fully air-gapped and only use a management plane for billing. we can produce a diagram of which telemetry is optional.
[06:20] Tom: any known regressions when switching model families for compatibility fallback? we saw different tokenization across a few open models which changed generation length.
[06:30] Omar: yes, tokenization mismatch is a gotcha. Redwood's runtime includes normalization layers to reduce variance, but when you fallback to a different family you should run a short A/B to confirm prompt drift.
[06:42] Priya: competitors question — we've had inbound from Anthropic and Vertex, what do you see as Redwood differentiator here?
[06:51] Maya: focus on production-first ops: transparent latency/unit-cost profiles, unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and the Optimize playbook that recommends batching and quantization config per workload.
[07:05] Derek: speaking of batching, we saw higher latency with aggressive batching during spikes. how does Redwood control batch sizes at tail?
[07:14] Omar: adaptive batching — it throttles based on target latency SLOs while opportunistically batching under load. you can pin max batch and per-tenant limits.
[07:26] Tom: can we get a dump of token distribution by route? that helped last quarter.
[07:31] Maya: yes we'll export per-route token histograms and top prompt templates.
[07:36] Priya: ok next steps recap?
[07:40] Maya: recap: Redwood sends pricing scenarios + security pack, Omar sends pilot config and schedule, Aurelia provides prompt sets and peak QPS windows, and we schedule a short sync after pilot results.
[07:53] Priya: thanks all.
[07:56] Maya: one more thing — for the pilot we'll also instrument quality regression alerts tied to a small eval suite to stop rollout if NER drops > 3%. we recommend that as a guardrail.
[08:10] Tom: good idea. we'll include NER tests in the evals.
[08:15] Maya: great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email.

(Transcript continues with some Q&A and minor cross talk)
[10:12] Tom: quick thing - the spike on Dec 12 correlated with a product experiment that increased system prompt length inadvertently.
[10:25] Maya: that explains the token jump; we can add alerts on median token-per-request to catch that early.
[10:35] Derek: and we'd like a playbook entry for rollback steps if a model variant causes generation quality issues.
[10:42] Omar: we'll attach our rollback checklist to the pilot doc.
[10:48] Priya: final ask, can you include an amortized cost model that shows breakeven point for Dedicated reserved vs pay-as-you-go?
[10:58] Maya: yes, i'll include amortization tables with sensitivity to QPS and token growth.
[11:05] Maya: ok meeting ends.

End of transcript.
